In terms of environmental impact, a city-by-city determination would afford a more exact method of achieving beneficial results. In juxtaposition to this view, however, is the argument that a city-by-city definition approach will require a significant number of individual adjudicatory proceedings which will cause administrative delays and a slower response to changing demographic patterns. Additionally, such an approach may create difficulty in carriers being able to perform within the given limits of a commercial zone, since a clear and precise method of definition will not be available.

It is evident that as the formula is modified to create expanded commercial zones, the potential for additional savings in mileage is increased. On the other hand, adoption of the above-suggested formula would create an even broader exempt market area, thus increasing the possibility of destructive competition and the possibility of adverse effect on short-haul carriers.
